01-a-setup.png.caption: **New Project** with Path of Radiance selected, the name *Tutorial Practice* and the parent folder. The preview line shows the folder the app will create.
01-a-setup.png.alt: New Project dialog: game choice, project name, Create in folder with Browse, folder preview, Create Project and Cancel buttons.

01-b-result.png.caption: Home of the extracted project: its name, game, platform and folder, the six section cards (Chapters lists 31 chapters, Characters 47 playable of 127) and **Changes this session**.
01-b-result.png.alt: Home page of Tutorial Practice with the Browse cards and the changes list.

01-c-extract.png.caption: **Disc & Patch** after **Choose disc image…**: the image is copied into the project's `source` folder and named on the **Source disc** card, *Not extracted yet*. **Extract** unpacks it; until then only Home and Disc & Patch open.
01-c-extract.png.alt: Disc and Patch page of an unextracted project with the source disc card, Choose disc image and Extract, and the disabled build and patch buttons.

01-d-tools.png.caption: **Settings › Disc and media tools…** (offered at first start when WIT is missing): **Download missing tools** fetches WIT, which extracts and builds discs, and, with **Include FFmpeg for audio/video imports**, FFmpeg. Your game files are not downloaded or included.
01-d-tools.png.alt: Set up disc and media tools dialog with the FFmpeg checkbox, Download missing tools and Later.

01-launcher.png.caption: The launcher when no project is open: **New project…** creates one, **Open project folder…** opens an existing one, and **Recent projects** lists the last ones opened.
01-launcher.png.alt: Tellius Modding launcher with New project, Open project folder and the empty recent projects list.

02-a-setup.png.caption: The workspace: section bar along the top, breadcrumbs with Back/Forward under it, the page, and the status bar with the unsaved count and **Changes this session**.
02-a-setup.png.alt: Home page showing the top section bar, search box, breadcrumb bar and status bar.

02-b-result.png.caption: **Ctrl+K** search for *Ike*: one list finds characters, classes, items, chapters and messages. Enter opens the selected result.
02-b-result.png.alt: Search palette over the workspace with the query Ike and matching results listed by kind.

02-c-crumbs.png.caption: The breadcrumb bar after Characters → Ike → Prologue: **‹** goes back to Ike (Alt+Left), **›** forward again (Alt+Right), and each crumb (*Chapters › Prologue: Mercenaries › Script*) is a link. The section tab in the top bar shows where you are.
02-c-crumbs.png.alt: Workspace on the Prologue Script tab with the breadcrumb bar and back and forward buttons.

02-d-back.png.caption: **‹** returned to Ike's Stats tab, as it was: pages keep their state while you move around, and unsaved edits stay in their editor.
02-d-back.png.alt: Ike's character page after pressing back, with the forward button now enabled.

03-a-setup.png.caption: An applied but unsaved edit: the form says **Unsaved changes in FE8Data.bin**, **Save FE8Data.bin** is enabled, and the status bar names the unsaved file.
03-a-setup.png.alt: Character Stats tab with the unsaved-changes warning beside Save FE8Data.bin and the unsaved count in the status bar.

03-b-result.png.caption: After saving, leaving and reopening the record, the Strength bonus is still raised and **Save FE8Data.bin** is disabled again: the file holds the value.
03-b-result.png.alt: Character Stats tab after reopening, with Save FE8Data.bin disabled and the raised Strength bonus.

03-c-changes.png.caption: **Changes this session** (the counter at the bottom left, or **View › Changes this session**): every save, import and restore of the session with its time and owner. It is not saved with the project.
03-c-changes.png.alt: Workspace with the Changes this session drawer open above the status bar, listing the saves.

04-a-setup.png.caption: **Settings › Preferences…**: **Dolphin location (Dolphin.exe)** is the emulator the app launches; Blender is optional and only used by the .blend model tools.
04-a-setup.png.alt: Preferences dialog with theme choice, Dolphin location and Blender location fields with Browse buttons.

04-b-result.png.caption: After **Build disc**: the status bar reads *Built* and the image path, the project's `build/Tutorial Practice.ciso`. Every build overwrites that file; open it in Dolphin, or use **Build and play in Dolphin**.
04-b-result.png.alt: Disc and Patch page after a build, with the built image path in the status bar.

04-c-build.png.caption: The **Build** card on Disc & Patch: **Build disc** packs the saved project files into a new image; **Build and play in Dolphin** also starts it.
04-c-build.png.alt: Disc and Patch page with the Build card showing Build disc and Build and play in Dolphin.

04-d-play-chapter.png.caption: **Play › Play chapter in Dolphin…** (F5): pick a chapter and a **Difficulty**; Dolphin starts on the extracted files, without a build, straight in that chapter.
04-d-play-chapter.png.alt: Play in Dolphin dialog with the chapter list, the difficulty choice, Play and Cancel.

05-a-setup.png.caption: **Tools › Check › Run check** on the unmodified project gives the baseline list. Note these rows: after an edit, only new rows are yours to fix.
05-a-setup.png.alt: Check page with the Run check button, the summary line and the results table.

05-b-result.png.caption: The file put back and **Run check** again: *0 errors, 4 warnings*, the baseline. The four warnings are in the retail data, in places the game never reaches.
05-b-result.png.alt: Check page back to the four baseline warnings and no error.

05-c-error.png.caption: An induced failure: with `Mess/C31.m` moved away, **Run check** reports *1 error*: **Severity** error, **Area** Chapter 31, **File** `Mess/C31.m`, *The chapter's message file is missing.* Double-click the row to open the chapter it belongs to.
05-c-error.png.alt: Check page with one error row for the missing message file of chapter 31 above the four baseline warnings.

06-a-setup.png.caption: The **Overview** of Ch.5: Flight! (slot 06). Under the title, the **Map phase** list (*Map phase 1 · bmap06*) with **‹ Phase** / **Phase ›**, **+ Phase…** and **Remove phase…**; on the right **▶ Play in Dolphin…**, **‹ Previous**, **Delete chapter…** and **Next ›**. The page lists the story flow, then the cast of each section of the Normal deployment file, here the 22 enemies of `bmap06_first_n` first.
06-a-setup.png.alt: Overview of Ch.5 Flight! with the map phase controls under the title, the Story flow box and the first section of the cast.

06-b-result.png.caption: Back on **Map phase 1 · bmap06**, the **Build** tab with the *Normal* file: the battle map with the 8 player slots, the 22 enemies of `bmap06_first_n` and the 5 reinforcements of `bmap06_zoen_n` on their tiles.
06-b-result.png.alt: Build tab of Ch.5 Flight! on the Normal deployment file with the unit markers on the map.

06-c-phase.png.caption: **Map phase 2 · bmap06_2** with **Deployment file** *Common*: the map of the opening cutscene. Its sections `bmap06_2_event00_c` and `bmap06_2_event_ged_c` are only placed by the script; its Normal, Hard and Maniac files are empty.
06-c-phase.png.alt: Overview of the second map phase of Ch.5 with the common deployment file's two event sections.

06-d-script.png.caption: The **Script** tab on `func_10`, the opening scene: `MapLoad("bmap06_2")` loads the cutscene map, `InstantDispos("bmap06_2_event00_c")` places its section, and `TalkEvent` plays the messages `MS_06_OP_01` and `MS_06_OP_02` of `c06.m`.
06-d-script.png.alt: Script tab of Ch.5 with the function list and the opening function that loads bmap06_2.

06-e-record.png.caption: The **Chapter data** tab: chapter 06's record in `FE8Data.bin`. **Map** `bmap06`, **Script** `C06`, **Message file** `C06` and the **Title key** `MCT06` are the names the other tabs follow.
06-e-record.png.alt: Chapter data tab of Ch.5 with the record's title key, map, script and message names and its other fields.

07-a-setup.png.caption: **Add chapter…**: **Copy of** Ch.1 (02), **Chapter number** 33, **Title** *Tutorial: Side Path*, **Played after** 02. The line under it says what changes: 02 will lead to 33, and 33 to 03.
07-a-setup.png.alt: Add Chapter dialog with Copy of, Chapter number, Title and Played after, the routing hint, Add Chapter and Cancel.

07-b-result.png.caption: Ch.1's **Story flow** after the add: its **Next chapter** is now *33 · Tutorial: Side Path*. The change is in `main.dol`'s next-chapter table; only playing Ch.1 to its end in Dolphin proves the transition.
07-b-result.png.alt: Story flow box of Ch.1 with Next chapter set to 33 Tutorial: Side Path.

07-c-flow.png.caption: The new chapter 33's **Overview**: **Played after:** *02 · Ch.1: The Battle Begins*, **Next chapter:** *03 · Ch.2: Rescue*, and **Take out of the story**, which only added chapters have. The header shows **Delete chapter…** for every chapter but the Prologue.
07-c-flow.png.alt: Overview of the added chapter 33 with its Story flow box, the Take out of the story button and the copied cast.

07-chapters.png.caption: **Chapters**: the action cards (**Add chapter…**, **New campaign…**, **Story order…**, **Create hub…**), then the story in play order with each chapter's place (*#1* to *#31*).
07-chapters.png.alt: Chapters page with the action cards and the story chapter cards with order badges.

07-d-order.png.caption: **Story order…**: retail chapters carry a lock and keep their place; the added chapter 33 sits between 02 and 03. **Move up** / **Move down** swap it only with another added chapter, so here they do nothing.
07-d-order.png.alt: Story order dialog with locked retail chapters and the unlocked chapter 33 selected between 02 and 03.

07-e-out.png.caption: After **Take out of the story**: *no chapter leads here: the game never reaches it*. Ch.1 leads to 03 again; chapter 33 and its files are still there, listed under **Other chapters**.
07-e-out.png.alt: Overview of chapter 33 after Take out of the story, with the unreachable note.

08-a-setup.png.caption: **New campaign…**: **Played after** the last story chapter (31, Endgame), three chapter rows (copies of 02, 03 with **Empty** ticked, and 04) and one row under **Characters (optional)**: `PID_TUTORIAL_SCOUT`, *Scout*, a copy of Boyd.
08-a-setup.png.alt: New campaign dialog with three filled chapter rows, one character row, Add chapter row, Add character row, Create campaign and Cancel.

08-b-result.png.caption: **Chapters** after **Create campaign**: the three new chapters close the story as *#32*, *#33* and *#34*, after Endgame.
08-b-result.png.alt: Chapters page scrolled to the end of the story with the three added chapter cards.

08-c-first.png.caption: The campaign's first chapter, 33 *Tutorial: Border Watch*, opens: **Played after** *31 · Endgame: Repatriation*, **Next chapter** *34 · Tutorial: The Ford*. Endgame no longer leads to the ending but to 33; 35 leads to the ending.
08-c-first.png.alt: Overview of chapter 33 Tutorial: Border Watch with its story flow from 31 to 34.

08-d-empty.png.caption: Chapter 34, made with **Empty**: the cast keeps only the player sections (*Player units*); the enemies of Ch.2 are gone, their sections kept empty so the copied script still finds them.
08-d-empty.png.alt: Overview of chapter 34 Tutorial: The Ford whose cast shows only the player units.

08-e-order.png.caption: **Story order…** after selecting 34 and **Move down**: the three added chapters can be reordered among themselves (here 33, 35, 34). **Apply** would rewrite the links; this run closes with **Cancel**.
08-e-order.png.alt: Story order dialog with the three unlocked added chapters at the end, 34 moved below 35.

08-f-cast.png.caption: The campaign's character `PID_TUTORIAL_SCOUT`: a copy of Boyd with its own name key `MPID_TUTORIAL_SCOUT` (*Scout*). No chapter deploys it yet.
08-f-cast.png.alt: Character page of PID_TUTORIAL_SCOUT with Boyd's class and stats and the name Scout.

10-a-setup.png.caption: **Characters › New character…**: the new PID is `PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD` and **Start as a copy of** is Boyd (`PID_BOLE`). The copy keeps Boyd's name key, portrait and class until you change them.
10-a-setup.png.alt: New character dialog with the new ID field, the copy-from list set to PID_BOLE, Create and Cancel.

10-b-result.png.caption: After **Apply** and **Save FE8Data.bin**, reopening the record: the page is titled *Guard*, **Save FE8Data.bin** is disabled and the HP bonus is kept. The record exists, but nothing deploys it yet.
10-b-result.png.alt: Character page of PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD titled Guard after saving, with its saved stats.

10-c-stats.png.caption: The new record after **＋ Create new message…** and before **Apply**: **Name key (MPID)** reads `MPID_TUTORIAL_GUARD` (*Guard*), the HP **Personal bonus** is raised from 6 to 7. The header still says *Boyd* and lists the records sharing his name until the file is saved.
10-c-stats.png.alt: Stats tab of PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD: identity, skills, map models, level row and the stat grid with the edited HP bonus.

10-d-deployment.png.caption: Placing it: on Ch.1's **Build** tab (*Normal*), Boyd's slot in `bmap02_mikata_n` selected and **Character** changed to `PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD`. **Apply**, then **Save Chapter**, writes the deployment file; this capture stops before **Apply**.
10-d-deployment.png.alt: Build tab of Ch.1 with a player unit selected and PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD in its Character field.

10-e-hub.png.caption: **Characters**, **All**, *Boyd* in **Search name or PID**: one card, Boyd, *+3 copies*. Records that share a name key are shown as one: Boyd's two event records and the new `PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD`, which still uses `MPID_BOLE`.
10-e-hub.png.alt: Characters page filtered on Boyd with the category chips, the count and the matching cards.

10-f-name.png.caption: **Name key (MPID)** › **＋ Create new message…**: **Message ID** `MPID_TUTORIAL_GUARD`, **Message text** *Guard*. **Create and assign** writes the text into `Mess/common.m` and points the record at it; Boyd keeps `MPID_BOLE`.
10-f-name.png.alt: Create message dialog with the message ID, the message text, Create and assign and Cancel.

10-g-unused.png.caption: **Appearances** of the new character: *Not found in any deployment file or chapter message.* Creating a record neither deploys nor recruits it.
10-g-unused.png.alt: Appearances tab of PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD with empty Deployed in and Dialogue tables.

11-a-setup.png.caption: **New portrait…**: name `TGUARD` (makes `FID_TGUARD` and `FID_L_TGUARD`), the nameplate key, **Use for character** `PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD`, and one body picture. Mouth and eye frames are optional; without them the face does not animate.
11-a-setup.png.alt: New portrait dialog with name, name key and character fields, the small and large portrait picture rows with Choose buttons, position spinboxes and the menu face row.

11-b-result.png.caption: `PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD`'s **Portrait & models** tab after **Create** and saving FE8Data.bin: the character resolves `FID_TGUARD`. This is the app's assembled preview, not the game.
11-b-result.png.alt: Portrait and models tab of PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD showing the new placeholder face and the model list.

11-viewer.png.caption: **Assets › Portraits** with `FID_IKE` selected: the pictures as the game assembles them, **Replace picture…**, and the **Face record (Face/facedata.bin)** with eye and mouth positions.
11-viewer.png.alt: Portraits page with the portrait list, the assembled face preview, replace controls and the face record form.

12-a-setup.png.caption: **New slot…** on `ymu/fighter`: **Copy animation ID** `AID_FIGHTER_BO` (Boyd's), **New animation ID** `AID_TGUARD`, **New folder** `tguard` (its own copy of the files), **Character** `PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD`, **Promoted model** off.
12-a-setup.png.alt: New slot dialog for a map model with the copied animation ID, new ID, new folder, character and promoted fields, Create and Cancel.

12-c-battle.png.alt: New slot dialog for a battle model with the model code, character and class fields.

12-d-look.png.caption: The Guard's **Portrait & models** after both slots: *Battle model* `zu/tgd1`, *Map model* `ymu/tguard` via `AID_TGUARD`. The promoted rows are unchanged: the slots were made for the unpromoted state only.
12-d-look.png.alt: Portrait and models tab of the Guard with its own battle and map models.

12-look.png.alt: Portrait and models tab listing battle model, promoted battle model, map model and promoted map model with their sources and Open in 3D Models buttons.

13-a-setup.png.alt: Supports tab with the partner list, affinity, thresholds per rank, conversation buttons and the bond section.

13-b-result.png.caption: Oscar's **Supports**: the same pair, written to both lists with the same thresholds, in the first empty slot of Oscar's list (2). Its **Bonus at A (each unit)** is *Attack +1, Hit +7, Avoid +15* (Fire with Earth). **Remove partner** on either side removes both and leaves the slots empty.
13-b-result.png.alt: Supports tab of Oscar with the new Guard pair selected among his partners.

13-c-pair.png.alt: Supports tab of the Guard with Oscar as partner, the thresholds and the conversation buttons.

14-a-setup.png.alt: Build tab of Ch.1 with an enemy bandit selected and PID_TUTORIAL_GUARD in its Character field.
